subject: Post-call: Podgest inference profile & topology readout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@podgest.ai>, Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@podgest.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Podgest inference profile & topology readout

Hi Samira / Ethan —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap so we have the same priorities and next steps. I kept this intentionally focused; let me know if I misunderstood anything.

Summary of pain and goals
- Current pain: unpredictable token latency during peak inference and high per-token compute cost for multi-tenant batch jobs.
- Business goal: serve Podgest’s summarization pipeline at 95th percentile latency <= 180ms for single-request interactive flows and sustained batch throughput of ~80k tokens/sec for nightly processing windows.
- Constraint: data must remain in their US cloud region; encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS is required.

Key technical notes from call
- Model family: Podgest will start with an open 7B LLM (family: regent-7b) and evaluate 13B variants. They plan to quantize to 4/4 or FP16 if quality permits.
- Typical input length: median request ~220 tokens; tail at ~1.2k for long-document summarization.
- Concurrent interactive users: ~120 during peak; batch jobs run 01:00–05:00 local time with heavy concurrency.
- Observability needs: token-level latency breakdowns and KV cache hit-rate metrics.

Deployment topology recommendation (high level)
- Private deployment in Podgest VPC (private control plane) with two availability zones:
  - Pool A: latency-optimized instances (A100 / H100) for interactive requests, autoscale 0–6 nodes with continuous batching tuned for 95ms median target.
  - Pool B: throughput-optimized nodes (8xA10G or equivalent) for batch windows; horizontal autoscaling policy based on queue depth and sustained token/sec.
- Smart routing policy: route interactive traffic to Pool A; fallback to smaller 13B quantized variant when A is saturated.
- Prefix/KV caching recommended for repeated-context workflows to reduce token compute.

Open risks / unknowns
- Exact latency characteristics for regent-7b after 4-bit quant; we should run an internal quant+perf sweep.
- Network egress pattern for batch windows — we asked for a traffic sample (please see attachment).

Next steps (owners & timing)
1) Redwood: run a small perf experiment (quant profiles + kernel selection) against your sample traffic — deliver by Fri 18 Apr. (owner: Ben)
2) Podgest: share a sanitized traffic sample and a recent model artifact for a quick repro. (owner: Samira)
3) Joint: 45-min follow-up to review perf findings + deployment sketch — proposed Wed 24 Apr 10am PT.

Attachments: podgest-traffic-sample.csv (sampled request stream), redwood-deployment-sketch.png (illustrative topology)

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Samira Khan <samira@podgest.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@podgest.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Podgest inference profile & topology readout

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear summary, that matches our notes. A couple clarifications and one addendum:

Clarifications
- The 95th perc target of <=180ms is for UI-facing single-shot summarization only; background async summarization can tolerate up to ~900ms.
- Our nightly batch runs actually consist of 3 staggered windows (01:00, 03:00, 05:00) each with different datasets; combined peak tokens/sec target is ~80–95k tokens/sec.

Addendum:
- We’ll attach the sanitized traffic sample to this thread later today (stripped of user ids). Also attaching a small model artifact (regent-7b-checkpoint.tar.gz) to a secure transfer link; Ethan will share the link here.

We’re comfortable with a private VPC deployment but would like to see the perf numbers before we commit to HA sizing.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform | Podgest, Inc.
samira@podgest.ai | +1 202-555-0147

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Podgest inference profile & topology readout

Karthik / Ben —

Thanks — quick internal alignment:
- Action: Ben to kick off quant+kernel sweep using a sampled subset from the attached CSV once Podgest uploads it. Please target both 4-bit (q4) and FP16 runs and capture 50/95/99pct latencies and tokens/sec.
- Ops: I’ll prep an initial private deploy estimate (nodes and storage) for the 3-window batch profile.
- Security: we need to confirm KMS integration pattern with Podgest’s cloud account — ask them for the KMS ARN in the follow-up.

I’ll aim to have the estimate and a quick ops checklist by Mon 15 Apr so we can review before the joint perf call.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com

Samira / Ethan —

Appreciate the quick confirmation. I’ll start the perf sweep as soon as we have the sample + model link. Expected deliverables from our side:
- Benchmark report (q4 + fp16) with 50/95/99 token latencies and tokens/sec 
- Suggested kernel/quantization profile that balances cost vs tail latency
- A draft private-deploy node-count estimate and cost ballpark for the initial pilot (monthly)

Tentative timeline: results and draft estimate by Fri 18 Apr. If you want to compress that, we can prioritize the interactive-flow numbers first (2–3 day turn).

Also, I can add a short pricing note to the report that maps pilots to reserved capacity vs hosted hybrid options.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 650-555-0123
